summary: Verified all 3 security-audit fixes: (1) rate limiting on POST /api/leads (5/IP/hour -> 429 with correct helpful message on 6th), (2) full removal of GET/POST /api/status (both now 404), (3) HTML-escaping of user-supplied fields (company/situation) before interpolation into the lead notification email HTML body, while raw values are still correctly persisted in MongoDB. Also regression-checked admin API key protection on GET /api/leads and /api/leads/count (401/401/200 as expected) and confirmed clean app startup (TTL index creation, no errors in backend logs). Frontend smoke tests: Minneapolis city page form, financial-it-support industry page form, homepage Business Technology Assessment (multi-step quiz + lead capture), Cyber Risk Scorecard (quiz + booking flow lead capture), and Human Risk Simulation game all loaded and functioned correctly with a single normal submission each (no rate limiting triggered).

issues: Pre-existing 'Download Our Free E-Book' modal pops up (sometimes repeatedly) and can overlay/block interactions with lower sections like the Human Risk Simulation game, requiring dismissal before clicking difficulty buttons. Not part of this security-audit fix batch, but worth noting as a UX friction point for the main agent.

action_items: No blocking action items from this security-audit fix batch - all 3 items (rate limiting, /api/status removal, HTML-escaping) verified working correctly.

Optional/non-blocking: consider suppressing or delaying the e-book download modal so it doesn't overlay interactive sections like the Human Risk Simulation game (pre-existing issue, not part of this fix batch).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is at 825 lines, mostly due to inline BLOG_POSTS content blocks - not a concern for this batch but worth splitting blog data into its own module file in a future cleanup pass (some already extracted into blog_data.py).
check_lead_rate_limit() correctly uses x-forwarded-for header with fallback to request.client.host - good practice for proxied deployments.
TTL index creation on startup is idempotent (create_index is safe to call repeatedly) and correctly scoped to LEAD_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS.

html.escape() correctly applied to all user-controlled fields (company, name, phone, email, situation, source, contact_preference) in _build_lead_html_body before HTML interpolation, and _sanitize_header_value() strips CR/LF from Subject header - both are correct, standard mitigations.
